supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Q^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ with $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb Q$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. For a rational power $q$, dimension powers mean $[X]^q=\ell^{qa}\tau^{qb}\mu^{qc}\vartheta^{qd}$ when $[X]=\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$. Rational exponents include the half-integer wave-function dimensions in clause (d); the integer-exponent dimensions form the subgroup $\mathbb Z^4$. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

For extensions using temperature, adjoin an independent dimension symbol $\Theta$: the enlarged group is $\mathbb Q^4\times\mathbb Q$, written $\ell^a\tau^b\mu^c\vartheta^d\Theta^e$, with the same componentwise rules. The preceding group embeds by $e=0$, so all previously assigned dimensions are preserved. Temperature has dimension $\Theta$, the Boltzmann constant has dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}\Theta^{-1}$, and entropy in joules per kelvin has that same dimension; a dimensionless entropy remains dimensionless. This convention does not assign a temperature or an entropy to any system.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres. In the temperature extension the reference unit of $\Theta$ is the kelvin (K), so the general reference unit gains a factor $\mathrm K^e$.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. These are real scalar constants with dimensions and units $[h]=[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (J s), $[c]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ (m s$^{-1}$), and $[e]=\vartheta$ (C). The vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is a positive real scalar that is experimentally determined in the current SI, with $[\mu_{0}]=\mu\ell\vartheta^{-2}$ (N A$^{-2}$ = H m$^{-1}$); $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$ is a positive real scalar with $[\varepsilon_{0}]=\mu^{-1}\ell^{-3}\tau^{2}\vartheta^{2}$ (F m$^{-1}$). These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: in the ordinary continuous-field regime, fix an integer $d\ge1$, an open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and an open time interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$. A **probability current density** is a declared continuous map $j:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^d$, whose spatial components have dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$ and reference unit $\mathrm m^{1-d}\mathrm s^{-1}$. At fixed time it is a spatial vector field; its signed normal component is read as probability transported per unit spatial $(d-1)$-area and time. Explicitly, for a flat face $S=\{x:x_k=a,\ a_i\le x_i\le b_i\ (i\ne k)\}\subset\Omega$, with $a_i<b_i$ and chosen normal $n=\epsilon e_k$, $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, define its **signed probability flux** at $t\in I$ as $\Phi_S(t):=\epsilon\int_{\prod_{i\ne k}[a_i,b_i]}j_k(x_1,\ldots,x_{k-1},a,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_d,t)\prod_{i\ne k}dx_i$. Here $e_k$ is the $k$th coordinate unit vector and the integral uses $(d-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure; for $d=1$ this means $\Phi_{\{a\}}(t)=\epsilon j(a,t)$. The flux has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ and unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$; positive sign means transport in the chosen normal direction. Fluxes through curved surfaces, or currents with weaker regularity, require separately specified surface measures or traces. This fixes the quantity type and flux convention; it supplies neither a current associated to an arbitrary $L^2$ state nor a conservation or detector law. Each dynamical model supplies its current construction and balance hypotheses.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, contraction maps
$\Psi_f^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$ and core operators $S_\pm(f)$ on the
finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For $f\in H$
define
$$D(A_+(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|P_+^{(n+1)}(f\otimes\psi_n)\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_+(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt n\,P_+^{(n)}(f\otimes\psi_{n-1})\ (n\ge1),\ (A_+(f)\psi)_0:=0,$$
$$D(A_-(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_-(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt{n+1}\,\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1}).$$
Put $D_1:=\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$. Then:

(a) $A_+(f)$ and $A_-(f)$ are well-defined linear operators on $F(H)$ with the
displayed domains, and they are the closure and the adjoint of the core operator:
$$A_+(f)=\overline{S_+(f)}=S_-(f)^*,\qquad A_-(f)=S_+(f)^*=\overline{S_-(f)}$$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) both $A_\pm(f)$ are closed, densely defined and satisfy
$A_+(f)^*=A_-(f)$, $A_-(f)^*=A_+(f)$; in particular $F_0\subseteq D_1\subseteq D(A_\pm(f))$;

(c) for every $\psi\in D_1$, $\|A_+(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$ and
$\|A_-(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$, where
$\|\psi\|_1^2=\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2$;

(d) for every $g\in H$ and $\psi\in D_1$ the identity
$$\|A_+(g)\psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\psi\|^2$$
holds.

No boundedness of $A_\pm(f)$ on $F(H)$, no self-adjointness of $A_\pm(f)$, and
no physical interpretation is asserted.

citations.quote:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is defined by the same bounded tensor maps and is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately. The finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment described by the finite open-system postulate is for $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$ with a fixed environment state and a declared joint unitary; it may be used for a separately selected finite-dimensional subsystem but does not cover the Fock field. A reduced-dynamics model involving the Fock field must separately specify a trace-class joint preparation and joint unitary on $\mathcal H_{AF}$. The trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)}:\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_{AF})\to\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_A)$ is defined for arbitrary Hilbert factors, is trace-norm contractive, and preserves positivity and trace by the mathematical partial-trace result listed below. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, fix a positive real action-scale parameter
$\hbar>0$, and let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.

Assume AC, $r\ge1$, and the finite-mode Fock conventions of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Let $U,V\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ obey
$$UU^*-VV^*=I_r,\qquad UV^T=VU^T,$$
where $^*$ is conjugate transpose and $^T$ is transpose without conjugation.
On the finite Hermite core define
$$a'_j=\sum_k(U_{jk}a_k+V_{jk}a_k^*).$$
Then the $a'_j$ satisfy $[a'_j,(a'_k)^*]=\delta_{jk}I$ and
$[a'_j,a'_k]=0$ on that core. The real matrix
$$S_g=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}(U+V)&-\operatorname{Im}(U-V)\\ \operatorname{Im}(U+V)&\operatorname{Re}(U-V)\end{pmatrix}$$
is symplectic in grouped coordinate order $(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r)$.
There is a unitary $M$ on finite-mode Fock, obtained by transporting an
individual finite symplectic implementer through the Fock–Schrödinger
unitary, such that $M^*aM=a'$ on the transported Schwartz core and
$M^*W(z)M=W(S_g^Tz)$ in grouped Weyl-label order. The transformed vacuum
$M\Omega$ has finite mean number
$$\sum_j\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=\operatorname{tr}(VV^*).$$
No infinite-mode implementability assertion is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

derivations.claim: The matrix $C$ is unitary because $C^*C=I_2$ follows from $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$. Its transpose $S=C^T$ is also unitary, so $U=S,V=0$ satisfy $UU^*-VV^*=I_2$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. By [F2] the finite-mode Bogoliubov statement supplies an implementer $M$ with $M^*aM=Sa$. Multiplying by $M$ and $M^*$ gives $MaM^*=S^{-1}a$; taking adjoints gives $Ma^*M^*=\overline{S}^{-1}a^*=S^Ta^*=Ca^*$ because $S$ is unitary and $S^T=C$. These identities hold on the transported finite-particle core.

The transformed vacuum has $\sum_{j=1}^2\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=0$ by [F2], so $a_1M\Omega=a_2M\Omega=0$. Expanding $M\Omega$ in the complete occupation basis [F1], the equation $a_1\psi=0$ forces every coefficient with first occupation $n_1>0$ to vanish by the ladder formula; $a_2\psi=0$ then forces every coefficient with $n_2>0$ to vanish. Hence $M\Omega=e^{i\phi}\Omega$ for some real $\phi$. Replacing $M$ by $U_C=e^{-i\phi}M$ preserves the conjugation identities and gives $U_C\Omega=\Omega$.

For $|n,0\rangle=(a_1^*)^n\Omega/\sqrt{n!}$, repeated use of the creation identity in [F1], the conjugation identity from step 1.1, and $U_C\Omega=\Omega$ from step 2.1 give $U_C|n,0\rangle=(t a_1^*+r a_2^*)^n\Omega/\sqrt{n!}=\sum_{k=0}^n\sqrt{\binom nk}t^k r^{n-k}|k,n-k\rangle$. The coefficient follows by choosing which $k$ of the $n$ commuting creation factors contribute $a_1^*$ and using $|k,n-k\rangle=(a_1^*)^k(a_2^*)^{n-k}\Omega/\sqrt{k!(n-k)!}$.

Orthogonality of the output occupation basis makes the joint ideal number-count probability the squared modulus of the coefficient in step 3.1. Since $|t|^2=\eta$ and $|r|^2=1-\eta$, for $0<\eta<1$ this is the displayed binomial law; at the endpoints the expansion has a single surviving basis vector. The declared number PVM and its Born rule [A1, F4] assign these probabilities.

By [F1, F3, F5], the families $|m,n\rangle$ and $|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$ are complete orthonormal families in $\mathcal F^{(2)}$ and $\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$, respectively. On finite sums define $\mathcal J_0\sum c_{mn}|m,n\rangle=\sum c_{mn}|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$; orthonormality makes its squared norm $\sum|c_{mn}|^2$, so it is well defined and inner-product preserving. For $\psi\in\mathcal F^{(2)}$, approximate by finite sums $\psi_j$ and define $\mathcal J\psi=\lim_j\mathcal J_0\psi_j$. The norm identity makes the images Cauchy in the complete product and the limit independent of the approximating sequence; it preserves linearity, norm and inner product. Its range is closed: if $\mathcal J\psi_j$ converges, the same norm identity makes $\psi_j$ Cauchy in the complete Fock space, so its limit maps to that range limit. The range contains the complete product family and hence is dense, so it is the whole product. This proves that $\mathcal J$ is unitary, uniquely fixed by the occupation map, with $\mathcal J\Omega=|0\rangle\otimes|0\rangle$. The coherent input series converges by [F3] and this unitary identification. Apply the bounded unitary $U_C$ to its norm-convergent partial sums. Each output occupation coefficient has only one contributing input total $n=k+\ell$; step 3.1 gives it as $e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\alpha^{k+\ell}t^kr^\ell/\sqrt{k!\ell!}$. The product of the two norm-convergent coherent series exists in the completed product by [F5]; approximating each factor by finite partial sums is legitimate since $\|u\otimes v-u'\otimes v'\|\le\|u-u'\|\|v\|+\|u'\|\|v-v'\|$. Its product-basis coefficients are the same, because $|t\alpha|^2+|r\alpha|^2=|\alpha|^2$. Completeness of that basis therefore proves $\mathcal J U_C|\alpha,0\rangle=|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$, retaining the exact vacuum phase and port convention.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is defined by the same bounded tensor maps and is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately. The finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment described by the finite open-system postulate is for $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$ with a fixed environment state and a declared joint unitary; it may be used for a separately selected finite-dimensional subsystem but does not cover the Fock field. A reduced-dynamics model involving the Fock field must separately specify a trace-class joint preparation and joint unitary on $\mathcal H_{AF}$. The trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)}:\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_{AF})\to\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_A)$ is defined for arbitrary Hilbert factors, is trace-norm contractive, and preserves positivity and trace by the mathematical partial-trace result listed below. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, fix a positive real action-scale parameter
$\hbar>0$, and let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions:
The two-mode occupation vectors $|n_1,n_2\rangle$ form a complete orthonormal basis and
$$a_1|n_1,n_2\rangle=\sqrt{n_1}|n_1-1,n_2\rangle,\quad a_2|n_1,n_2\rangle=\sqrt{n_2}|n_1,n_2-1\rangle,$$
$$a_1^*|n_1,n_2\rangle=\sqrt{n_1+1}|n_1+1,n_2\rangle,\quad a_2^*|n_1,n_2\rangle=\sqrt{n_2+1}|n_1,n_2+1\rangle,$$
with annihilation zero when its corresponding occupation is zero. The creators commute and the annihilators kill $\Omega$ ([[lem-nrqmx-finite-mode-fock-schr-identification]]). historical_source_interface.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $r\ge1$, let $H=\mathbb C^r$ with orthonormal basis
$e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal F_s(H)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes_s n}$
be the bosonic Fock space with vacuum $\Omega$ and creation and annihilation
operators $a_j^*,a_j$ from
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] and
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For
$N=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb N_0^r$, set
$$|N\rangle:=\prod_{j=1}^r\frac{(a_j^*)^{n_j}}{\sqrt{n_j!}}\Omega.$$
Let $g_N(x)=\prod_{j=1}^r g_{n_j}(x_j)$ be the normalized product Hermite
function from [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]].
Then $(|N\rangle)_N$ and $(g_N)_N$ are complete orthonormal families, and the
map $\mathcal U|N\rangle=g_N$ extends uniquely to a unitary
$$\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^r)\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^r).$$
On the algebraic finite-particle span, $\mathcal U a_j\mathcal U^{-1}$ and
$\mathcal U a_j^*\mathcal U^{-1}$ are respectively
$(x_j+\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ and $(x_j-\partial_{x_j})/\sqrt2$ on product
Hermite functions. In particular the quadratures
$$Q_j=\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j+a_j^*),\qquad P_j=-i\sqrt{\hbar/2}(a_j-a_j^*)$$
act there as multiplication by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ and as
$-i\sqrt\hbar\,\partial_{x_j}$, respectively. These are core identities;
they do not assert that a finite number cutoff preserves the canonical
commutation relations.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume AC, $r\ge1$, and the finite-mode Fock conventions of
[[def-nrqmx-finite-mode-symplectic-data]]. Let $U,V\in M_r(\mathbb C)$ obey
$$UU^*-VV^*=I_r,\qquad UV^T=VU^T,$$
where $^*$ is conjugate transpose and $^T$ is transpose without conjugation.
On the finite Hermite core define
$$a'_j=\sum_k(U_{jk}a_k+V_{jk}a_k^*).$$
Then the $a'_j$ satisfy $[a'_j,(a'_k)^*]=\delta_{jk}I$ and
$[a'_j,a'_k]=0$ on that core. The real matrix
$$S_g=\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Re}(U+V)&-\operatorname{Im}(U-V)\\ \operatorname{Im}(U+V)&\operatorname{Re}(U-V)\end{pmatrix}$$
is symplectic in grouped coordinate order $(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r,P_1,\ldots,P_r)$.
There is a unitary $M$ on finite-mode Fock, obtained by transporting an
individual finite symplectic implementer through the Fock–Schrödinger
unitary, such that $M^*aM=a'$ on the transported Schwartz core and
$M^*W(z)M=W(S_g^Tz)$ in grouped Weyl-label order. The transformed vacuum
$M\Omega$ has finite mean number
$$\sum_j\|a_jM\Omega\|^2=\operatorname{tr}(VV^*).$$
No infinite-mode implementability assertion is made.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions: The one-mode coherent vector has the normalized expansion $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_n\alpha^n|n\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$, and the occupation vectors are orthonormal ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]]).

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.
