citations.quote:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is defined by the same bounded tensor maps and is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately. The finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment described by the finite open-system postulate is for $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$ with a fixed environment state and a declared joint unitary; it may be used for a separately selected finite-dimensional subsystem but does not cover the Fock field. A reduced-dynamics model involving the Fock field must separately specify a trace-class joint preparation and joint unitary on $\mathcal H_{AF}$. The trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)}:\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_{AF})\to\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_A)$ is defined for arbitrary Hilbert factors, is trace-norm contractive, and preserves positivity and trace by the mathematical partial-trace result listed below. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the finite-mode assignment with two modes and its ideal number PVM, with AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the implementer and completed Fock/tensor suppliers. Write $\mathcal F^{(2)}=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^2)$ in the ordered mode basis $(1,0),(0,1)$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. The mode-factorization map is the unitary $\mathcal J:\mathcal F^{(2)}\to\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$ determined by $\mathcal J|m,n\rangle=|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$. Here $\widehat\otimes$ is the completed Hilbert tensor product, and the one-mode occupation vectors and their products use the same vacuum and mode order. Its unitary extension is proved below. Let $t,r\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless amplitudes with $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$, and fix the complete unitary mode matrix $C=\begin{pmatrix}t&-\overline r\\r&\overline t\end{pmatrix}$. Use the state-action convention that the passive unitary $U_C$ satisfies $U_C\Omega=\Omega$, $U_Ca_1^*U_C^*=t a_1^*+r a_2^*$, and $U_Ca_2^*U_C^*=-\overline r\,a_1^*+\overline t\,a_2^*$ on the finite-particle core. Put $\eta:=|t|^2$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and $0\le k\le n$, write $\binom nk:=n!/(k!(n-k)!)$. For input $|n,0\rangle$ and $0<\eta<1$, the joint output count law is
$$\mathbb P(k,\ell)=\begin{cases}\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k},&\ell=n-k,\ 0\le k\le n,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
At $\eta=0$ and $\eta=1$ the joint laws are respectively point masses at $(0,n)$ and $(n,0)$. Thus the first output count is binomial with parameters $(n,\eta)$. For a dimensionless coherent input $|\alpha,0\rangle$ with $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$, define $|\alpha,0\rangle=\mathcal J^*(|\alpha\rangle\otimes|0\rangle)$, equivalently $e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n,0\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$. The output state under this fixed mode factorization is $\mathcal J U_C|\alpha,0\rangle=|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$; on $\mathcal F^{(2)}$ it is $\mathcal J^*(|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) read the projective rules of P3, and the finite-outcome law in (d) reads P2(iv). Clause (d) additionally stipulates the countably infinite nonprojective outcome law, generalized conditional and discarded-outcome updates, and abstract-instrument law and updates as assumptions of each declared apparatus model, as permitted by P3(v)'s requirement for separate models outside its projective class. These are not consequences of P1-P3 alone. Clauses (e)-(f) fix the declaration discipline and limits used by the page's later items. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and for $u,v\in H$ let $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) For every bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]),

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

with the Hilbert adjoint $B^*$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then for every bounded $B$

$$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

both series converging absolutely with $\bigl|\operatorname{tr}(BT)\bigr|\le\|B\|\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|$, and $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). In particular $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$. No cyclic permutation of unbounded operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.

derivations.claim: For $0\le\eta\le1$, direct multiplication gives $C_\eta^*C_\eta=C_\eta C_\eta^*=I_2$, so the full unitary-matrix hypothesis of the beam-splitter theorem holds. The product occupation vectors $|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$ form a complete orthonormal family by the product-basis result of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], and the two-mode occupation vectors $|m,n\rangle$ form a complete orthonormal family by [[lem-nrqmx-finite-mode-fock-schr-identification]]. Therefore the basis map defining $\mathcal I$ preserves inner products on a dense subspace and has dense range; it extends uniquely to a surjective isometry, hence a unitary. Also, the vacuum insertion $V_0\psi=\psi\otimes|0\rangle$ is an isometry by the elementary-tensor norm identity of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. For each finite-dimensional ancilla $\mathbb C^q$, $W_q:=I_q\otimes V_0$ is an isometry by [F6]. If $T\ge0$ is trace class, then $W_qTW_q^*\ge0$ because $\langle W_qTW_q^*x,x\rangle=\langle T W_q^*x,W_q^*x\rangle\ge0$. For arbitrary trace-class $T$, write $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ as a nuclear series by [F5]. Directly from the rank-one definition and the adjoint identity, $W_qT_{u_j,v_j}W_q^*x=\langle W_q^*x,v_j\rangle W_qu_j=\langle x,W_qv_j\rangle W_qu_j=T_{W_qu_j,W_qv_j}x$. The resulting rank-one series converges in trace norm since $\sum_j\|W_qu_j\|\|W_qv_j\|=\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<\infty$, and its operator-norm sum is $W_qTW_q^*$. Since $W_q$ preserves inner products, [F5]'s rank-one trace formula gives $\operatorname{tr}(W_qTW_q^*)=\sum_j\langle W_qu_j,W_qv_j\rangle=\sum_j\langle u_j,v_j\rangle=\operatorname{tr}T$. Thus adjoining vacuum is completely positive and trace-preserving.

For each finite ancilla $\mathbb C^q$, the amplification of the partial-trace map is, after the canonical unitary reassociation from [F6], the partial trace over the environment Fock space on $\mathbb C^q\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. By [F2] it maps positive trace-class operators to positive trace-class operators and preserves their trace. Therefore the partial trace is completely positive and trace-preserving under [F3].

For $0<\eta<1$ and input $|n\rangle\langle n|$, [F1] gives the joint pure state $\sum_{k=0}^n c_k|k\rangle\otimes|n-k\rangle$ with $c_k=\sqrt{\binom nk}\eta^{k/2}(1-\eta)^{(n-k)/2}$. Expanding its rank-one density and applying the rank-one partial-trace formula [F2], cross terms with $k\ne\ell$ vanish because $\langle n-\ell,n-k\rangle=\delta_{k\ell}$. The reduced state is $\sum_k|c_k|^2|k\rangle\langle k|$, which is the displayed mixture; its ideal number-PVM law is the binomial distribution by the declared outcome model [A1].

For input $|\alpha\rangle\langle\alpha|$, [F1] gives the product output $|t\alpha\rangle\langle t\alpha|\otimes|r\alpha\rangle\langle r\alpha|$. The rank-one partial-trace formula [F2] leaves the first factor unchanged; with $t=\sqrt\eta$, this is $|\sqrt\eta\,\alpha\rangle\langle\sqrt\eta\,\alpha|$.

At $\eta=0$, the transported beam-splitter expansion [F1] gives $\widetilde U_0(|m\rangle\otimes|0\rangle)=|0\rangle\otimes|m\rangle$ for every $m\in\mathbb N_0$; at $\eta=1$ it gives $\widetilde U_1(|m\rangle\otimes|0\rangle)=|m\rangle\otimes|0\rangle$. The finite linear span of the one-mode occupation basis is dense by [F4], so boundedness of the unitaries extends these identities to $\widetilde U_0(\psi\otimes|0\rangle)=|0\rangle\otimes\psi$ and $\widetilde U_1(\psi\otimes|0\rangle)=\psi\otimes|0\rangle$ for all one-mode vectors $\psi$.

Conjugation by $\widetilde U_\eta$ is completely positive because unitary conjugation preserves positivity on every finite ancilla amplification. It preserves trace for every trace-class input by [F5], since $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde U_\eta T\widetilde U_\eta^*)=\operatorname{tr}(T\widetilde U_\eta^*\widetilde U_\eta)=\operatorname{tr}T$; by [F6], $I_q\otimes\widetilde U_\eta$ is unitary and the same identity holds on every finite ancilla amplification. Composition with step 1.1 preserves both properties.

By steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1, the composition defining $\Phi_\eta$ maps trace-class operators to trace-class operators, is completely positive under every finite ancilla, and preserves trace. It is CPTP on the full infinite-dimensional one-mode trace-class space; no finite-dimensional Choi theorem is used.

For rank-one $T_{u,v}$, the partial-trace formula [F2] applied to the two isometries in step 1.5 yields $\Phi_0(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle|0\rangle\langle0|=\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})|0\rangle\langle0|$ and $\Phi_1(T_{u,v})=T_{u,v}$. By [F5], every trace-class input has a nuclear series of rank-one terms converging in trace norm. The partial trace is trace-norm contractive by [F2], and bounded isometric and unitary conjugations are trace-norm continuous by [F5]; the trace is trace-norm continuous by [F5]. Passing to the limit gives $\Phi_0(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho)|0\rangle\langle0|$ and $\Phi_1(\rho)=\rho$. In particular these are vacuum and identity on density operators.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
**(a) Finite oscillator-mode data.** Choose an integer $M\ge1$, the one-particle mode space $\mathfrak h=\mathbb C^M$ with a declared orthonormal mode basis $e_1,\ldots,e_M$, and the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ with vacuum $\Omega$. Here $\mathfrak h^{\otimes_s n}$ is the range of the orthogonal symmetrizer in the completed $n$-fold Hilbert tensor product, with the zero-particle sector $\mathbb C\Omega$. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_M)\in\mathbb N_0^M$, let $|\mathbf n\rangle$ be the normalized occupation vector. Define the finite-particle subspace $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}:=\{\psi=(\psi^{(n)})_{n\ge0}\in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h):\psi^{(n)}=0\text{ for all but finitely many }n\}=\operatorname{span}\{|\mathbf n\rangle:\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M\}$. The mode operators are dimensionless and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $a_j|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j}|\mathbf n-\mathbf e_j\rangle$ and $a_j^*|\mathbf n\rangle=\sqrt{n_j+1}|\mathbf n+\mathbf e_j\rangle$, with the first expression zero if $n_j=0$. The Fock space is infinite-dimensional for each $M\ge1$; no particle-number cutoff or tensor factorization of an individual photon into position and spin is part of this assignment.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice wherever the finite-mode Fock, quadrature, and implementability suppliers require them. These are mathematical hypotheses of the assignment, not physical postulates.

**Mode-frequency data.** Use $\hbar>0$ for the reduced Planck constant in joule-seconds under the framework's SI convention. For each selected mode $j$, choose a positive angular frequency $\omega_j>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$; the assigned one-quantum energy scale is $\hbar\omega_j$ joules. These are parameters of the finite-mode model, not measured frequencies.

**(b) Finite atom and dipole data.** Choose $d\ge1$, an atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, a Hermitian atomic energy matrix $H_A$ in joules, Hermitian compressed dipole matrices $D_j$ in coulomb-metres, and real mode field scales $\mathcal E_j$ in volts per metre. The matrix elements of $G_j:=\mathcal E_jD_j/\hbar$ have units seconds$^{-1}$, where $\hbar>0$ is retained in joule-seconds. The finite matrices and scales are chosen model data. If they are obtained by compressing a larger atomic model, that compression's error is a separate model input and is not bounded here.

Write $\mathcal H_{AF}:=\mathcal H_A\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$ for the completed ordered Hilbert tensor product, with the atom factor first, and let $\kappa:\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the canonical isometric inclusion. Let $I_A$ and $I_F$ denote the identity operators on $\mathcal H_A$ and $\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)$. Let $\mathcal D_0:=\kappa[\mathcal H_A\odot\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}]\subseteq\mathcal H_{AF}$ be the algebraic product domain. If $f_1,\ldots,f_d$ is the standard orthonormal basis of $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^d$, then the vectors $\kappa(f_\alpha\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle)$ form a complete orthonormal basis by the Hilbert tensor product and finite-mode Fock product-basis conclusions for this ordered pair. Hence $\mathcal D_0$ is dense in $\mathcal H_{AF}$.

The assigned dipole interaction is the linear operator $V_{\mathrm{dip}}:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal H_{AF}$ defined on elementary tensors by $V_{\mathrm{dip}}(\kappa(\phi\otimes\psi)):=-\sum_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal E_j\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ for $\phi\in\mathcal H_A$ and $\psi\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$, and extended linearly to $\mathcal D_0$. Each map $(\phi,\psi)\mapsto\kappa(D_j\phi\otimes(a_j+a_j^*)\psi)$ is bilinear, so it descends to the algebraic tensor product; $a_j,a_j^*$ preserve $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$. Each summand has units joules. This is the declared algebraic product domain of the finite-core expression; no graph-core assertion for a closed realization is made. The assignment does not assert that an arbitrary such sum has a self-adjoint realization or generates an evolution; any dynamical use must state and justify its operator domain. The Jaynes–Cummings supplier below gives one specific self-adjoint direct-sum realization.

**(c) Mode transformations.** A finite mode-coordinate change is assigned only when its finite Bogoliubov matrices satisfy the exact hypotheses of the finite-mode implementability statement: for $U,V\in M_M(\mathbb C)$, $UU^*-VV^*=I_M$ and $UV^T=VU^T$. The resulting unitary acts on this finite-mode Fock space. The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice; this is a mathematical assumption, not a physical law. No infinite-mode implementability follows.

**(d) Detector outcome models.** A detector's outcome space $(X,\Sigma)$ and POVM $E:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{AF})$ are declared model data: each $E(B)$ is bounded and positive, $E(X)=I$, and $E$ is countably additive in the weak operator topology. For a density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ (a positive trace-class operator of trace one), the assigned probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ under the framework's stated measurement convention. An ideal number-resolving model on the field has outcomes $\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^M$ and effects $I_A\otimes|\mathbf n\rangle\langle\mathbf n|$; these are bounded tensor maps and projections on $\mathcal H_{AF}$ by the tensor-map adjoint and composition rules. For ideal homodyne of mode $j$ at phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$, let $R_j(\theta)|\mathbf n\rangle=e^{i\theta n_j}|\mathbf n\rangle$ and $X_{j,\theta}:=\hbar^{-1/2}R_j(\theta)Q_jR_j(\theta)^*$, where $\mathcal U:\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^M)\to L^2(\mathbb R^M)$ is the Fock-to-Schrödinger unitary and $Q_j:=\mathcal U^{-1}M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}\mathcal U$. Here $M_{\sqrt\hbar x_j}$ multiplies by $\sqrt\hbar x_j$ on its maximal domain $\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^M):x_jf\in L^2(\mathbb R^M)\}$. Thus $X_{j,\theta}$ is self-adjoint by unitary conjugation and on $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{fin}}$ equals $(e^{-i\theta}a_j+e^{i\theta}a_j^*)/\sqrt2$. Its spectral PVM $B\mapsto I_A\otimes\mathbf1_B(X_{j,\theta})$ is defined by the same bounded tensor maps and is the ideal homodyne POVM on the product space. These are ideal outcome assignments, not claims about a detector's optical local oscillator, efficiency, bandwidth, calibration or state update. If a state update or a finite detector environment is modeled, declare its instrument separately. The finite product-preparation/unitary/partial-trace assignment described by the finite open-system postulate is for $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$ with a fixed environment state and a declared joint unitary; it may be used for a separately selected finite-dimensional subsystem but does not cover the Fock field. A reduced-dynamics model involving the Fock field must separately specify a trace-class joint preparation and joint unitary on $\mathcal H_{AF}$. The trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h)}:\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_{AF})\to\mathcal S_1(\mathcal H_A)$ is defined for arbitrary Hilbert factors, is trace-norm contractive, and preserves positivity and trace by the mathematical partial-trace result listed below. No Fock-field reduced dynamics or reservoir limit is adopted here.

**(e) Optional approximation regimes.** A long-wavelength identification with a spatial electromagnetic mode requires a separately declared atomic extent $L$ and wave number $k_j$ and the scale regime $k_jL\ll1$; no error bound is supplied. A rotating-wave choice keeps only the excitation-exchange terms. For a two-level transition of frequency $\omega_0$ coupled to a mode of frequency $\omega$, its usual low-excitation regime is $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ on the declared photon-number sectors; it is not uniform over the full Fock space. A Markov/GKSL approximation is another separate model choice and must state its rates, reservoir correlation time $\tau_B$, system time scale $\tau_S$, and regime $\tau_B\ll\tau_S$. None of these optional approximations is derived from this assignment or from the finite system-environment model.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the finite-mode assignment with two modes and its ideal number PVM, with AC and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the implementer and completed Fock/tensor suppliers. Write $\mathcal F^{(2)}=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C^2)$ in the ordered mode basis $(1,0),(0,1)$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. The mode-factorization map is the unitary $\mathcal J:\mathcal F^{(2)}\to\mathcal F\widehat\otimes\mathcal F$ determined by $\mathcal J|m,n\rangle=|m\rangle\otimes|n\rangle$. Here $\widehat\otimes$ is the completed Hilbert tensor product, and the one-mode occupation vectors and their products use the same vacuum and mode order. Its unitary extension is proved below. Let $t,r\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless amplitudes with $|t|^2+|r|^2=1$, and fix the complete unitary mode matrix $C=\begin{pmatrix}t&-\overline r\\r&\overline t\end{pmatrix}$. Use the state-action convention that the passive unitary $U_C$ satisfies $U_C\Omega=\Omega$, $U_Ca_1^*U_C^*=t a_1^*+r a_2^*$, and $U_Ca_2^*U_C^*=-\overline r\,a_1^*+\overline t\,a_2^*$ on the finite-particle core. Put $\eta:=|t|^2$. For $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and $0\le k\le n$, write $\binom nk:=n!/(k!(n-k)!)$. For input $|n,0\rangle$ and $0<\eta<1$, the joint output count law is
$$\mathbb P(k,\ell)=\begin{cases}\binom nk\eta^k(1-\eta)^{n-k},&\ell=n-k,\ 0\le k\le n,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
At $\eta=0$ and $\eta=1$ the joint laws are respectively point masses at $(0,n)$ and $(n,0)$. Thus the first output count is binomial with parameters $(n,\eta)$. For a dimensionless coherent input $|\alpha,0\rangle$ with $|\alpha\rangle=e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$, define $|\alpha,0\rangle=\mathcal J^*(|\alpha\rangle\otimes|0\rangle)$, equivalently $e^{-|\alpha|^2/2}\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha^n|n,0\rangle/\sqrt{n!}$. The output state under this fixed mode factorization is $\mathcal J U_C|\alpha,0\rangle=|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle$; on $\mathcal F^{(2)}$ it is $\mathcal J^*(|t\alpha\rangle\otimes|r\alpha\rangle)$.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions: For arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces $H,K$, the trace-class partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ is trace-norm contractive, preserves trace and positivity, and on rank-one tensors satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}_K T_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle T_{u,u'}$; its proof assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]]).

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Here the projective outcome law is supplied directly by P3(ii), and the finite-effect law by P2(iv); no spectral PVM is constructed from an assigned self-adjoint observable. The additional Axiom of Choice required by P2(ii) for that construction is therefore not used here. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms. For a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, expanding $\langle D(x+ty),x+ty\rangle\ge0$ with $t=-\langle Dx,y\rangle/\langle Dy,y\rangle$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle>0$, and varying $t\in\mathbb C$ when $\langle Dy,y\rangle=0$, gives $|\langle Dx,y\rangle|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle Dy,y\rangle$. Since $0\le D\le I$, taking $y=Dx$ yields $\|Dx\|^4\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\langle D(Dx),Dx\rangle\le\langle Dx,x\rangle\|Dx\|^2$, hence $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$ (also when $Dx=0$). The partial sums therefore converge on every $x$ and their limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. For finite $A$ this is clause (iv) of P2, even if an outcome has countably many Kraus operators. For countably infinite $A$ outside the projective case of (a)-(b), we explicitly adopt this same probability law as an additional assumption of the declared apparatus model; P2(iv) does not state that extension. The Kraus-normalization lemma establishes that these numbers are nonnegative and sum to one, not that they describe physical outcomes. The model also explicitly stipulates the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. These update series converge in trace norm by the Kraus-normalization lemma, with grouping permitted by absolute trace-norm convergence for positive inputs. Their interpretation as post-measurement states is part of the instrument declaration; P3 supplies that interpretation only for its projective Lueders case. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$. The interpretation of these formulas as an outcome law and a post-measurement state is likewise an explicitly adopted assumption of this abstract apparatus model. [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]] establishes the effect duality, countably additive normalization and well-definedness of the positive-probability conditional state, not this physical interpretation. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and for $u,v\in H$ let $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) For every bounded $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]),

$$BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v},\qquad T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v},$$

with the Hilbert adjoint $B^*$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]).

(b) Let $T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class and let $T=\sum_jT_{u_j,v_j}$ be a nuclear representation, i.e. the partial sums converge to $T$ in operator norm and $\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|<\infty$ ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then for every bounded $B$

$$\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\sum_j\langle Bu_j,v_j\rangle,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(TB)=\sum_j\langle u_j,B^*v_j\rangle,$$

both series converging absolutely with $\bigl|\operatorname{tr}(BT)\bigr|\le\|B\|\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\|$, and $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). In particular $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$. No cyclic permutation of unbounded operators is asserted.
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions: For trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$, $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$, and every trace-class input has a nuclear rank-one series convergent in trace norm ([[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,H',K,K'$ be complex Hilbert spaces and let $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ be bounded linear operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Write $H\widehat\otimes K$ for the completion of the algebraic tensor product constructed in [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], with inclusion $\kappa$.

(a) There is a unique bounded linear operator $S\otimes T: H\widehat\otimes K\to H'\widehat\otimes K'$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u\in H$, $v\in K$, and it satisfies $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]).

(b) For Hilbert spaces $H'',K''$ and bounded $S':H''\to H$, $T':K''\to K$, one has $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$. In particular, for endomorphisms $S:H\to H$, $T:K\to K$, the endomorphisms $S\otimes I_K$ and $I_H\otimes T$ commute and their composite is $S\otimes T$.

(c) The Hilbert adjoint ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]) is $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$.

(d) If $S,T$ are unitary, then so is $S\otimes T$. No extension of unbounded maps, and no algebraic manipulation of domains of unbounded operators, is asserted.
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions: Bounded maps tensor to bounded maps on the completed Hilbert tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]). For finite-dimensional $\mathbb C^q$, expand in an orthonormal basis of the first factor to see $I_q\otimes J$ preserves norm whenever $J$ does; the reassociation of three factors preserves the elementary-tensor inner products and therefore extends by density to a unitary, using the completion construction ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

Take the one-mode, two-level specialization of the finite-mode assignment and use its SI convention with $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. Let $\omega>0$ be the selected angular frequency in seconds$^{-1}$, let $\mathcal H_A=\mathbb C^2$ have orthonormal states $|g\rangle,|e\rangle$, and choose $\omega_0>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$, $d\in\mathbb R$ in coulomb-metres, and $\mathcal E\in\mathbb R$ in volts per metre. Set $\sigma_+=|e\rangle\langle g|$, $\sigma_-=|g\rangle\langle e|$, $\sigma_z=|e\rangle\langle e|-|g\rangle\langle g|$, and $\sigma_x=\sigma_++\sigma_-$. Choose $H_A=(\hbar\omega_0/2)\sigma_z$ and $D=d\sigma_x$; then the dipole expression $-\mathcal E D\otimes(a+a^*)$ has energy units. Define the real coupling $g:=-\mathcal E d/\hbar$ in seconds$^{-1}$. Retaining from the dipole expression just the excitation-exchange terms $\sigma_+\otimes a$ and $\sigma_-\otimes a^*$ gives coefficient $-\mathcal E d=\hbar g$. Thus the rotating-wave Hamiltonian below is a specified specialization of the model assignment, not an independently measured interaction.

Let $\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$ be the infinite-dimensional one-mode bosonic Fock space with occupation basis $|n\rangle$, $n\in\mathbb N_0$, and operators $a|n\rangle=\sqrt n|n-1\rangle$, $a^*|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}|n+1\rangle$ on the finite-particle core. Write $I_A$ and $I_F$ for the identity operators on the atomic and field factors, respectively. Define $\Delta=\omega_0-\omega$. For this rotating-wave model, whose usual scale $|g|\sqrt{n+1}\ll\omega,\omega_0$ applies only to the photon-number sectors under study and is not uniform over the full Fock space, set
$$H_{\rm core}=\hbar\omega\,I_A\otimes a^*a+\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{2}\sigma_z\otimes I_F+\hbar g(\sigma_+\otimes a+\sigma_-\otimes a^*)$$
on the finite-particle core of $\mathbb C^2\widehat\otimes\mathcal F_s(\mathbb C)$. The Hamiltonian is the exact operator for the selected rotating-wave model; no error bound relative to the unapproximated dipole interaction is asserted.

The total excitation operator $N_{\rm exc}:=I_A\otimes a^*a+\sigma_+\sigma_-\otimes I_F$ is conserved on that core. The ground line $\mathbb C|g,0\rangle$ is invariant. For each $n\in\mathbb N_0$, the subspace $\mathcal K_n=\operatorname{span}\{|e,n\rangle,|g,n+1\rangle\}$ is invariant and the restriction has matrix
$$H_n=\begin{pmatrix}\hbar\omega n+\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{2}&\hbar g\sqrt{n+1}\\\hbar g\sqrt{n+1}&\hbar\omega(n+1)-\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{2}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its eigenvalue splitting is $\hbar\sqrt{\Delta^2+4g^2(n+1)}$. Define the full Hamiltonian to act on the ground line by $-\hbar\omega_0/2$ and as the orthogonal direct sum of the $H_n$ on the $\mathcal K_n$, with squared-block-norm domain
$$D(H_{\rm JC})=\left\{c|g,0\rangle\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\psi_n:\ c\in\mathbb C,\ \psi_n\in\mathcal K_n,\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|H_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
This direct-sum operator is self-adjoint and extends $H_{\rm core}$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statement of isolated autonomous dynamics. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which are the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and group suppliers.

**(i) Energy operator.** An **isolated autonomous system** of the sector has a declared **energy operator** $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ that is self-adjoint ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and a declared energy unit in which its spectral coordinate is read. The energy operator is part of the model specification of the system; for a massive particle it is fixed by the kinematics postulate P5, and singular or unbounded model Hamiltonians require their own self-adjointness statements.

**(ii) Evolution.** The time evolution of the model is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$
defined by the spectral calculus of the self-adjoint generator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The energy unit enters the argument of the exponential so that $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ acts in the dimensionless spectral variable.

**(iii) State evolution.** A vector state evolves continuously, $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the Schroedinger equation
$$i\hbar\,\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi(t)$$
holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$, where the derivative is the norm limit of the difference quotients; for other vectors the equation is not asserted, although the evolution remains continuous. A density-operator preparation evolves as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$, which is a density operator for every $t$ and satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

**(iv) Time-dependent families.** A prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators is a different model assumption: a norm-continuous finite-dimensional Hermitian family is used only through the unitary two-time propagator that its family defines, and the exponential of the integral of $H(t)$ is not identified with that propagator unless the family commutes with itself at different times. The general unbounded time-dependent case requires a separate existence and domain theorem of its own and is not adopted by this postulate; the driven-dynamics page states its own assumptions for the models it treats.

**(v) Open systems.** A non-unitary evolution of the reduced description of a system coupled to an environment is an extension obtained from an explicitly chosen environment model and a declared reduction, not a replacement for clause (ii); no environment model is adopted by this postulate.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the isolated-system idealization. They assert nothing about the origin of the energy operator of a concrete system, about the accuracy of the idealization for a laboratory preparation, or about which laboratory interactions realize an isolated evolution; those are tested identifications in the sense of P7.

**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.
